prompt:
USE: Square album-cover artwork test. Artwork only, no lettering.

SCENE: A dark stone ledge after rain, at night.

SUBJECT: One pale rose lying on the wet stone, lower third of the frame.

DETAILS: Light: Light: fog and soft diffuse light, no hard shadows, haze and depth. Medium: Medium: black and white film snapshot shot with direct flash, grain and small dust specks.

COMPOSITION: Keep the top 30% quiet: no strong edges or highlights, reserved for type added later.

REFERENCES:
- Image 1: our own earlier draft. Redraw it at full quality: keep its subject, shapes and layout, then apply THIS ROUND.

BRAND: An image in the visual world of Inch of Shadow, a Berlin artist. The name comes from the line "one inch of love is one inch of shadow": love and shadow, light and dark. Mood: romantic, melancholic, mysterious, refined.

Everything in the image completes as one whole. Every element belongs; nothing is random or added on.

The light always has one clear idea: a direction, a glow, haze, a flash or a shadow. Never flat, even, commercial light.

Do not add people unless the subject asks for them. When a person is in the image, their attitude is distant and self-possessed, supremely confident, out of reach, sexy in a tasteful way, never explicit. If a real person is in the image, keep their face exactly as it is.

No logos, no watermarks, no text or letters anywhere in the image.

CONSTRAINTS: No text or letters anywhere. No logos, no watermark. No people.

THIS ROUND: Redraw Image 1 with exactly one change: Replace the SCENE line with: "SCENE: A dark stone ledge after rain, at night, with only deep black fog behind it. No buildings, no domes, no towers, no street lights, no far shore." Keep everything else as it is in Image 1: the same subject, layout, light, palette and texture.
subject: One pale rose lying on the wet stone (test render)
fix: Replace the SCENE line with: "SCENE: A dark stone ledge after rain, at night, with only deep black fog behind it. No buildings, no domes, no towers, no street lights, no far shore."

review.summary: The rose, the quiet black fog and the empty top area work well, and there are no buildings or text. But the ledge reads as glossy, crinkled black plastic or draped fabric rather than stone, which breaks today's rule for matte surfaces touched by time.

issues.note: The ledge does not read as stone. Its front edge folds like draped cloth, and the top looks like crumpled wet plastic or foil.
The ledge has a high-gloss, glittery sheen with many tiny specular sparkles. Today's brand core asks for matte stone and nothing glossy or plastic.

review.prompt_fix: Replace "One pale rose lying on the wet stone" with "One pale rose lying on a rough, matte, weathered stone ledge with a hard squared edge, only damp, a few raindrops, no shiny sheen".
